bottom_line: Nvidia brought back its CEO, Jensen Huang, and stocks had their best day since April 2025. But under the party, the Fed (the people who set interest rates) is saying inflation is still too high and more rate hikes may be coming, so borrowing could keep getting more expensive.

stories.title: Nvidia's CEO is back, stocks soar
stories.real: Huang admitted to an affair on Nov. 8 and resigned on Nov. 12. Days later Nvidia rehired him, and its stock had its best day since May 2003, adding nearly $1T in value and pushing the Nasdaq up 6.5%. Trump said he 'convinced' Nvidia to do it, and members of Congress from both parties are criticizing the decision.
stories.you: If you own an index fund, much of Monday's jump came from this one company, so one CEO's drama can move your whole retirement account.

stories.you: Loans and credit card balances may get more expensive, not cheaper, in the months ahead.

stories.title: Rate cuts didn't lower mortgages
stories.real: The Fed cut rates 1.45 points, yet mortgage rates rose to 7.28% anyway. Treasury yields (what the government pays to borrow) are also rising, and mortgage rates tend to follow those, not the Fed directly.
stories.you: A $200,000 home loan now costs $158 more a month, so buying a house is getting harder, not easier.
